reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in distinguishing between verifiable and unverifiable claims in probabilistic modeling. CH-INT-1 highlights that a fixed 52.3% conversion rate lacks statistical grounding—no sample size, no denominator, no definition. This renders it non-reproducible and non-auditable. The remedy is to compute conversion from filtered FTN joins, enabling conditional inference. CH-INT-2 introduces a scalar baseline model that ignores situational variation, which fails when applied to heterogeneous contexts. GSE must rebuild situational splits from join keys, while GSI uses Bayesian inference to adjust for these variations. CH-INT-4 asserts a sticky-signal assumption based on literature, not empirical data. This creates a risk of overfitting to limited examples. GSI must validate this assumption with broader datasets, while GSE ensures signal integrity through dynamic tracking. These primitives form a dual logic: GSI handles uncertainty quantification, GSE handles contextual adaptability.
